title: Phase 4: Threat Intelligence onto the app shell
description:
## Goal
Move Threat Intelligence (Amplify app d3on1y5vlrxmam, https://threat-intelligence.anth.us, Pretext reader + its own CMS backend, pre-production) from a hand-made fork deployment onto the standard template pattern proven on Pilobol.us: a publication repo on the published packages (@anthusai/papyrus, papyrus-newsroom) with papyrus.config.ts and amplify/backend.ts, infra/site.json to the CDK app shell (repo-less Amplify app, GitHub App connected in the console), a NEW backend, content copied across, Google sign-in, domain move to the SAME hostname with rollback, staging, retire the old app, docs. Purpose: dogfood the new backend CMS UX (the /newsroom Shadcn app) on a low-stakes site before converting anth.us.

## Why this is bigger than "theme and config"
See the assessment comment. In short: the brand/theme/pictograms/video theme are config-sized, but the fork also carries ~1,700 lines of a Pretext blog layout engine (rhythm, feature solver, header, overlays) that does not exist in Papyrus develop, brand fonts wired in app/layout.tsx, and live content in DynamoDB/S3 that has diverged from the Git seed (6 of 18 articles).

## Sub-tasks (label phase-4), dependency order
P4-01 baseline capture; P4-02 upstream blog engine (pure modules); P4-03 upstream blog components and brand slots; P4-04 TI publication repo scaffold; P4-05 template: shared-root domain and staging name; P4-06 new CMS app from the template, GitHub App connect, first build; P4-07 Google sign-in and first admin; P4-08 content copy tool and dry run; P4-09 apply copy, convert bodies, fidelity check; P4-10 staging and dogfood publish flow; P4-11 domain move with rollback; P4-12 retire old app, backend, secrets; docs and procedures.
Parallel at the start: P4-01, P4-02, P4-05.

## Done when
threat-intelligence.anth.us is served by the new app from a repo that depends on pinned Papyrus packages, content matches the baseline, editors sign in with Google to the new /newsroom, staging shows drafts to editors only, and the old app, stack, secrets and fork-only code are retired.

## Not in scope
Anth.us conversion, p.apyr.us product site (separate Phase 4 ticket PPY-d1cc15: note the numbering clash, see the assessment), research/knowledge-graph data migration (open question Q4), moving to a shared multi-tenant backend (rejected by epic decision 2).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
ASSESSMENT (2026-10-07, read-only research; nothing executed, no AWS or repo changes).

## What TI is
- Amplify app d3on1y5vlrxmam, WEB_COMPUTE, repo anthusai/threat-intelligence (AnthusAI/Threat-Intelligence, a GitHub FORK of Papyrus, public). Single branch main, last build 2026-08-29 = repo main 9058211. Console-pasted build spec (npm install, ampx pipeline-deploy, next build). Branch env var NAMES: NEXT_PUBLIC_PAPYRUS_SITE_BRAND, PAPYRUS_SITE_BRAND (threat-intelligence), PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE, PAPYRUS_EDITION_SLUG, PAPYRUS_ENABLE_CONSOLE_RESPONDER=false, PAPYRUS_ENABLE_SLACK=false, PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET (a plain-text env var: its value is exposed by get-app; rotate, never reuse).
- Public site is Pretext 'blog' layout co-hosted with /newsroom in the one app. https://threat-intelligence.anth.us redirects / to /2026/july/04; 18 articles at /2026/july/04/<slug>; /articles, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt are 404.
- Domain: domain association anth.us, prefix threat-intelligence, branch main. Route 53 zone Z02552332GG6AM25SFP73 has a CNAME (TTL 500). The anth.us root is also associated with app d2hbn1ig6nqyhy (Anth.us live), so one root domain sits on two apps today.
- Fork vs Papyrus: merge base 95df656 (2026-07-02); 81 commits ahead, 306 behind develop (213 behind main). Diff 126 files, +35k/-19k. Papyrus develop was already partly de-forked (brands register from papyrus.config.ts, VideoML pipeline moved into papyrus_content/videoml, IAM auth).

## Theme/config vs real code
Ryan's premise ("just a different front-end configuration and a custom theme") holds for the publications/ part (40 of the 126 changed files) and the storybook files (26, dropped), and NOT for the remaining ~50 core files.
- Config/theme (stays in TI repo): brand (publications/threat_intelligence/brand.ts), theme.css 2,144 lines + theme-newsroom.css 195, pictograms (art, figure, registry, system), blog-defense header art, TI video scene components (title slide, quote card, rhythm, pictogram video, browser/preview bundles), seed content JSON, skills, docs, corpora/*.yml (9 files, 39 KB), public brand assets (5.4 MB).
- Real code that exists ONLY in the fork (not on Papyrus develop): lib/blog-rhythm.ts (134), lib/blog-feature-solver.ts (459), components/presentation-header.tsx (138), presentation-rhythm-hrule.tsx, use-rhythm-overlay.ts; reworked presentation-shell (+375), article-page (+312), archive-shell, globals.css (+259), plus article routes passing videoScript/sections, getCachedVideoScript in the content repository, brand fonts loaded in app/layout.tsx (Inter masthead, IBM Plex Serif body) and article-video.tsx (+272). About 1,700 lines of TS plus CSS. These must be upstreamed into the Pretext renderer (standard-site.md 3.2 already says so) because SiteBrand.components has only PictogramFigure and BlogPageBackground slots and no font slot.
- Superseded, do not port: VideoML pipeline Python and scripts (now papyrus videos + brand.video slot), auth redirect JSON/publication-redirects (now backend.auth.redirectUrls), JWT authorizer (removed from develop), storybook, console-fix docs and scripts.
- The fork's schema delta is auth only (guest read), which develop has: no data-model divergence.

## Backend facts (old stack amplify-d3on1y5vlrxmam-main-branch-aeb7dfa526 plus nested stacks, 39 DynamoDB tables, ~a dozen Lambdas)
- Content: Item 20 (18 published, 2 private editorial-doctrine), PublishedItem 18, Edition 1, EditionItem 18, Published* 1/18, MediaAsset 24, ItemTag 24, Tag 8, NewsroomSection 6.
- Research/knowledge data: Reference 1866, SemanticRelation 3258, SemanticNode 387, Message 907, ReferenceAttachment 626, ModelAttachment 585, Assignment 67, AssignmentEvent 42, ProcedureRun 25, KnowledgeRawPayload 155, KnowledgeImportRun 23, procedure definitions/versions 8 each, KnowledgeCorpus 1, plus an S3 Vectors bucket.
- S3 media bucket 1004 objects, 254 MB: media/ 65 (160 MB; 14 mp4 incl. two 26 MB edition videos, 13 svg), corpora/ 409 (88 MB, source PDFs/HTML: NOT in Git), newsroom/ 530 (5.6 MB payloads).
- Cognito pool us-east-1_lAtce7ZTu: 2 users (1 CONFIRMED, 1 EXTERNAL_PROVIDER), groups admin 1, editor 2; Google IdP present, auto-generated domain b1f1d3a11a4545ba5318, callbacks threat-intelligence.anth.us and the amplifyapp URL. Google sign-in on the old site is expected broken (Ryan removed its URIs, epic comment 4e3a16). SSM secrets: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, PAPYRUS_JWT_SECRET.
- Features: console responder off, Slack off; inbound email and storage backups not deployed (no TI SES rule, no backup plan, no EventBridge rules; SES rule set belongs to p.apyr.us). The Lambdas for those features exist in the stack but are not wired. So the template's four feature flags can all be false, as Pilobol.us.
- Ingestion: nothing scheduled. Content came from the Git seed JSON via seed tooling and was then edited in the DB: 6 of 18 live articles differ from the Git seed (the DB is the authority).

## Template and package gaps (evidence)
1. Blog layout engine not in Papyrus (above); no brand font slot (app/layout.tsx on develop loads only Playfair and Plus Jakarta; slots limited to PictogramFigure, BlogPageBackground).
2. Domain model: template emits AWS::Amplify::Domain {domainName: cms.domainName, prefix ""}; TI's association is root anth.us + prefix threat-intelligence on a root shared with another app: unverified whether the full-host form works. Derived staging host would be staging.anth.us (resolveStagingDomainName replaces the first label): collides with Anth.us staging; must set cms.stagingDomainName explicitly.
3. Pretext publish -> live: pages use revalidate 3600; on-demand /api/revalidate needs PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET as both an Amplify backend secret (backend revalidateBaseUrl) and a frontend runtime env var. site.json is public (no secrets) and console-set branch variables are wiped by the next stack update (and by console connect). No secret-safe path exists in the template.
4. No backend-to-backend content copy command. papyrus ops content has import-markus, export-published (article/page only, Markus build dir), convert-bodies, publish and friends. A round trip through Markus would drop Pretext fields (section, deck, dateline, byline, pullQuotes, editorial, layout, editionDate).
5. Template builds a reader app only for markus-static; for Pretext the example has no reader block: correct for TI (no gap), but `PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_*` is the Pretext analogue of rebuild-on-publish (gap 3).
6. Pilobol lessons carry over: console connect flips platform, replaces the service role, deletes branches and env vars; Google secrets and Cognito prefix as above; the new Cognito domain must differ from the old pool's.

## Data migration approach
Content lives in DynamoDB and S3, not Git. New backend (fresh schema from develop, legacy body fields still valid) + one-off, idempotent copy of the content models and media/ prefix from the OLD API (IAM/SigV4) into the new one with id, slug and key preservation, dry run first (P4-08); then convert-bodies --apply (bodyMarkus/bodyIr; fails closed unless paragraphs round-trip exactly) and a fidelity gate against the P4-01 baseline (P4-09). Users are not migrated (2 people): they sign in with Google and get groups. Research/knowledge data is NOT copied by default (Q4); the old backend is retained until sign-off.

## Phase 4 plan (label phase-4, children of this ticket)
P4-01 PPY-a01095 baseline capture (no AWS write). P4-02 PPY-c6f967 upstream blog engine (pure modules). P4-03 PPY-4eb02e upstream blog components + brand slots. P4-04 PPY-504020 TI repo scaffold on packages + infra/site.json (Ryan: disable old app auto-build first). P4-05 PPY-67226e template: shared-root domain + staging host. P4-06 PPY-4f2519 new CMS app from template, GitHub App connect, first build, gates (Ryan: SSO, stack yes, console sitting). P4-07 PPY-153434 Google sign-in + first admin (Ryan: Google console URIs, secrets, sign-in). P4-08 PPY-26f158 content copy tool + dry run. P4-09 PPY-301b12 apply copy, convert bodies, fidelity gate (Ryan yes). P4-10 PPY-80f2dc staging + dogfood publish flow (Ryan). P4-11 PPY-386123 domain move with rollback (Ryan go/no-go). P4-12 PPY-ff500e retire old app/backend/secrets, fork-only code, docs (Ryan deletions, merges).
Order: P4-01, P4-02, P4-05 start together; 02>03>04>06>07/08>09>10>11>12. Estimates (agent-days): 0.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 1, 1.5, 0.5, 2, 1, 1.5, 1, 1.5 = 18 total, critical path about 16 (02,03,04,06,08,09,10,11,12), plus a sign-off period. Biggest uncertainties: blog-layout upstream fidelity (P4-02/03) and Amplify accepting the prefix on a shared root (P4-11).

## Risks
Visual drift from the blog engine upstream; domain claim on a root shared with Anth.us (rollback command in P4-11; never touch d2hbn1ig6nqyhy); merging the scaffold to the fork's main rebuilds the OLD app and breaks it unless auto build is disabled first (P4-04); editing in the old CMS during the copy window; research data lost if the old stack is deleted before Q4 is decided; Google client unverified-domain limit.

## NUMBERING NOTE
Epic 1f1489 already has PPY-d1cc15 titled 'Phase 4: p.apyr.us product site...'. This ticket uses the requested title and label phase-4; the two share the number. Suggest Ryan renumber one (for example this as Phase 3b, since it completes Phase 3's de-fork item). PPY-3367d3 (Phase 3) lists Threat Intelligence in its title but has no TI sub-tasks: this ticket supersedes that part; no TI-specific tickets existed to re-parent (PPY-b794e1 'Migrate Papyrus + Threat Intelligence content to Markus Markdown bodies' is open under PPY-92f846 and only overlaps on pull-quote placement, left alone).

## OPEN QUESTIONS FOR RYAN
Q1 Cutover style: hard cutover with brief downtime (as Pilobol.us), with the old app and backend kept until sign-off? Rollback is a domain re-association.
Q2 Repo: keep AnthusAI/Threat-Intelligence (a fork; scaffold replaces its contents, history kept, tag pre-standard-fork) or a new repo? Detach the GitHub fork link (needs GitHub support)?
Q3 Confirm the scope surprise: TI is config PLUS ~1,700 lines of blog-layout code to upstream into Papyrus (recommended, matches epic decision 3) rather than keeping layout overrides in the TI repo (needs new Papyrus override hooks).
Q4 Research/knowledge data (references, graph, messages, assignments, corpora PDFs 88 MB): migrate, or archive and drop? Recommendation: copy published content only now, archive the rest (S3 sync + DynamoDB export) before deleting the old stack.
Q5 Confirm the live DB (not the Git seed) is authoritative for the 6 diverged articles.
Q6 Brand fonts: add a small font slot in Papyrus (recommended) or load them from the publication CSS?
Q7 Publish-to-live latency: accept hourly ISR, or build a secret-safe on-demand revalidate path?
Q8 Staging hostname under anth.us: staging.threat-intelligence.anth.us, or no custom staging domain (amplifyapp URL)? staging.anth.us is taken by Anth.us.
Q9 Freeze editing in the old /newsroom between P4-08 and P4-11? Who are the 2 editors to add?
Q10 Sign-off period length before deleting the old app (recommend 7 days).

comments.author: home
comments.text: DECISIONS (Ryan, 2026-10-07, "go with defaults"): 1 hard cutover with brief downtime; keep old app+backend until sign-off. 2 keep repo AnthusAI/Threat-Intelligence, detach the fork link, scaffold on main; old code stays in Git history under a tag. 3 upstream the ~1,700 lines of Pretext blog layout code into Papyrus. 4 research/knowledge data: archive (export to S3, keep old backend), do not migrate. 5 live database wins for the 6 diverged articles. 6 brand fonts from the publication CSS, no new Papyrus font slot. 7 accept hourly page refresh for now; secret-safe on-demand revalidate is a later follow-up. 8 explicit staging host (e.g. threat-intelligence-staging.anth.us), not the derived staging.anth.us. 9 freeze edits in the old newsroom during the copy window; the 2 editors are still to be named by Ryan (needed at P4-07). 10 two-week sign-off before deleting the old app and backend. Also: rotate PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET at cutover; the new backend must not reuse it.

comments.author: home
comments.text: SCOPE UPDATE (Ryan, 2026-10-07): the Papyrus improvements identified during planning are IN SCOPE for this phase, not deferred. This supersedes decisions 6 and 7 above: brand fonts get a real slot in Papyrus (P4-03), and secret-safe on-demand revalidation is built now (new ticket below) instead of accepting hourly refresh. Template/package gaps found (shared-root-domain host and explicit staging host, no backend-to-backend copy tool, console-connect side effects) stay in the plan as written.

comments.author: home
comments.text: GOOGLE DECISION (Ryan, 2026-10-07): the shared Google OAuth project 94722830066 was the wrong project in the wrong Google account and has been shut down. Per-site Google projects/clients from now on (Pilobolus already has its own: project 472527967203). Threat Intelligence gets a NEW Google project + OAuth client; its Cognito domain origin/redirect URI go on that client and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET come from it. This supersedes the "one shared OAuth client" assumption in the Phase 4 plan and P4-07. Fallout of the shutdown found 2026-10-07 (project numbers read from SSM client IDs): new Pilobol.us CMS dv0pdx67fk80m, old TI app d3on1y5vlrxmam and Papyrus app dbsyytcm9drqa (p.apyr.us) all pointed at the dead client; Anth.us production has no Google client in this store.

right_now_summary: The new TI app is built and content is copied; Ryan’s reviews and domain cutover remain.
